newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Electrabel says gearing for competition.
newsitem.headline: Electrabel says gearing for competition.

text.p: Belgian power utility Electrabel said on Monday it was gearing up for increasing competition in electricity supply markets as liberalisation progressed and new technology made possible smaller, efficient generating plants.
The European Union has agreed that 30 percent of national electricity supply markets must be open to competition from 2006.
This opening is to be phased in over three stages each lasting three years.
Electrabel Chief Executive Jean-Pierre Hansen said Belgium's existing relative openness was no reason for complacency.
"We must not lose sight of the fact that the real driving force behind competition in the electricity sector in Europe lies elsewhere," he told the company's annual meeting.

"Namely in the evolution of technologies such as smaller, lighter and less capital-intensive generation units which is encouraging the appearance of new potential players and competition on the ground that has little to worry about from planned deregulation or agreements between countries.
"Moreover, the relative saturation of the various national markets and customers' expectations...make sharp growth in competition inevitable," he said.

In order to meet this competition Electrabel had begun streamlining and refining its services and its structure, and commissioning new generating plants to replace existing elderly conventional units, Hansen said.
Two new steam and gas turbine plants would come on stream by the end of this year, and another would be ready by the end of 1998, he noted.

Electrabel also had a part stake in two new nuclear power plants in France that sre scheduled to enter service later this year. The company was also renovating its existing nuclear and conventional generating plants.

Hansen also later told reporters there was an unspecified possibility for synergies with Belgian holding company Tractebel from the planned merger between France's Lyonnaise des Eaux and Tractebel parent Compagnie de Suez.
Suez currently holds 63 percent of Belgian holding company SGB which in turn owns 65 percent of Tractebel, which is itself a large shareholder in Electrabel.
"At the moment Tractebel simply has a financial stake in Electrabel. If the merger goes ahead it will also be a potential operator, even a competitor," Hansen said.
"It is not excluded that on the ground there could be synergies," he added.
However, Hansen said Electrabel was not involved in any discussions at present.
